beginner.summary: No Snowflake experience assumed. Participants learn the Snowflake architecture, warehouses, loading and querying data (including JSON), Time Travel and cloning, access control, Snowpipe, streams and tasks, sharing and cost control, and build a small analytics pipeline.
prerequisites: Comfortable writing basic SQL (SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY)
A Snowflake trial account or trainer-provided sandbox
outcomes: Explain Snowflake's architecture and run queries in Snowsight
Load, query and model structured and JSON data
Use Time Travel, cloning and role-based access control
Automate loading with Snowpipe, streams and tasks and control cost

course_outcomes.outcome: Explain Snowflake architecture and work in Snowsight
Size and run virtual warehouses
Create databases, schemas and tables
Load data with stages, file formats and COPY
topics: Loading Data: Stages, File Formats and COPY

course_outcomes.outcome: Query relational data with SQL
Query JSON with VARIANT
Use views and explain the caching layers
Recover data with Time Travel and clone it without copying
Control access with roles
Load data continuously with Snowpipe and automate it with streams and tasks
Share data securely and control credits with resource monitors
topics: Managing Cost: Credits and Resource Monitors

course_outcomes.outcome: Deliver a small analytics pipeline

subtopics: Separation of storage, compute and cloud services
Choosing a cloud provider and region
Snowsight worksheets, roles and warehouse selector
Query context: ROLE, WAREHOUSE, DATABASE, SCHEMA
Running a query and reading the result grid
Getting help and documentation in Snowsight
days.lab_task: Log in to Snowsight, set your role and warehouse, run three queries against SNOWFLAKE_SAMPLE_DATA, and note where storage, compute and services each do their work.
days.deliverable: Worksheet with three working queries and a short note mapping each query step to a layer
checks: Both return the values set in context
Rows return without creating any table
Ask which layer stores the data
Participant names the storage layer, separate from compute
objectives: Navigate Snowsight and set query context
Run queries against shared sample data

subtopics: Warehouse sizes and credit consumption per second
Starting, suspending and resizing a warehouse
Local data cache on a warehouse
days.lab_task: Create an XS warehouse with auto-suspend of 60 seconds, run the same aggregation on XS and S, and record the runtime and credits for each.
days.deliverable: Table comparing XS vs S runtime and credits for the same query, with a sizing recommendation
checks: Set auto-suspend to 60s and leave the warehouse idle
It suspends and consumes no credits while idle
Run the aggregation on XS then S
The larger size finishes faster for this query
Credit use matches the size and active time
objectives: Choose a size from measured evidence

subtopics: Primary, unique and foreign key constraints (informational)
UNDROP and the role of Time Travel
days.lab_task: Model a small sales schema (customers, orders, order_items), create the tables with sensible types and constraints, then drop and UNDROP one table.
days.deliverable: SQL script that creates the schema and demonstrates UNDROP of a table
checks: All tables exist with correct data types
The table and its data return
objectives: Design a schema and choose data types
Recover a dropped table with UNDROP

days.topic: Loading Data: Stages, File Formats and COPY
subtopics: The COPY INTO command and options
Compression and file sizing for load speed
days.lab_task: Load a provided CSV of 10,000 orders through an internal stage with a defined file format, send bad rows to a rejection path, and verify the load count.
days.deliverable: Loaded ORDERS table, a file format object, and a report of accepted versus rejected rows
checks: Row count equals the file's data rows
COPY a file with three bad rows using ON_ERROR=CONTINUE
Good rows load, three are rejected
objectives: Stage files and define a file format

subtopics: SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY and HAVING
The result cache and when it applies
days.lab_task: Answer five business questions on the sample sales data using joins, a window function and a CTE, and show that re-running an identical query hits the result cache.
days.deliverable: Worksheet with five answered questions and evidence of a cache hit
checks: Compute each customer's running total with a window function
Running totals are correct per customer
Re-run an identical query within the cache window
It returns from cache with near-zero compute
Rank the top five products per month
Results match a manual check on a sample month
objectives: Write analytical SQL with joins and windows

subtopics: The VARIANT, OBJECT and ARRAY types
Loading JSON into a VARIANT column
Casting extracted values to typed columns
days.lab_task: Load a JSON file of web events into a VARIANT column, extract user, event type and timestamp into a typed view, and flatten an array of items.
days.deliverable: A typed view over the raw JSON and a flattened item-level query
checks: Extract event_type and cast the timestamp
Values are correctly typed, not VARIANT
One row per item with the parent event id
objectives: Load and query JSON with VARIANT

subtopics: When to use each kind of view
days.lab_task: Build a reporting view over the sales schema, convert it to a secure view, and demonstrate warehouse-cache versus result-cache behaviour.
days.deliverable: A reporting view, a secure variant, and notes on which cache served each query
checks: It returns the expected joined result
Make it secure and inspect its definition as a lower-privilege role
The definition is hidden from that role
Run a query cold, warm and identical
Each run uses a different cache, shown in the profile
objectives: Protect query logic with secure views

subtopics: AT and BEFORE clauses (offset, timestamp, statement)
Zero-copy cloning of tables, schemas and databases
Clones for test and dev environments
Storage of clones and changed micro-partitions
days.lab_task: Corrupt a table with a bad UPDATE, recover it with Time Travel, then create a zero-copy clone of the schema for a test environment.
days.deliverable: Recovered table and a cloned test schema, with a note on storage cost of the clone
checks: Run a bad UPDATE then restore with AT(OFFSET)
The clone appears instantly and shares storage
SHOW SCHEMAS and a storage note
Change a row in the clone
Only the changed micro-partitions add storage; source is untouched

subtopics: System roles: ACCOUNTADMIN, SYSADMIN, SECURITYADMIN, USERADMIN, PUBLIC
Granting roles to users and to other roles
days.lab_task: Create an ANALYST role that can read the sales schema only, assign it to a test user, and prove the user cannot write or see other schemas.
days.deliverable: Role and grant script, assigned to a test user, with proof of least privilege
checks: Grant SELECT on the sales schema to ANALYST
The user can read sales tables
Attempt an INSERT as the user
Add a future grant for new tables
A newly created table is readable without a new grant
objectives: Create custom roles with least privilege

subtopics: PIPE objects and their COPY statement
days.lab_task: Create a Snowpipe that loads new files from an external stage, drop two files in, and confirm they load automatically within the latency window.
days.deliverable: A working pipe and a monitoring query showing auto-loaded files
checks: The pipe exists and is running
Add two files to the stage
Both load without a manual COPY
Credits and files loaded are reported

subtopics: Combining a stream with a task
WHEN conditions to skip empty runs
days.lab_task: Capture inserts to a staging table with a stream, and schedule a task that merges new rows into a target table every minute.
days.deliverable: A stream, a scheduled task, and evidence that new rows flow to the target
checks: Insert rows into the staging table
The stream shows the new rows as changes
New rows appear in the target and the stream clears
The task shows successful scheduled runs

subtopics: Sharing a database with a share
days.lab_task: Create a share that exposes one read-only view of the sales data, and describe how a consumer account would query it without copying data.
days.deliverable: A share object with one view and a one-paragraph explanation of consumer access
checks: Create a share and add a secure view
The share lists only the intended view
The share is ready for a consumer to mount
Participant states the data is not copied to the consumer
objectives: Create a share with a secure view

days.topic: Managing Cost: Credits and Resource Monitors
subtopics: Credit model for compute and cloud services
days.lab_task: Create a resource monitor that suspends a warehouse at a monthly credit quota and alerts at 80 percent, then verify the alert and suspend actions.
days.deliverable: A resource monitor with thresholds and evidence of its actions
checks: Set a monitor at a small quota with an 80% alert
Monitor is attached to the warehouse
The warehouse is suspended by the monitor
objectives: Explain the credit and storage cost model

days.lab_task: Build a pipeline that ingests raw orders (COPY or Snowpipe), transforms them with a task, exposes a secure reporting view to an ANALYST role, and runs under a resource monitor.
days.deliverable: A working end-to-end pipeline with RBAC, cost control and a short demo
checks: Load raw data and transform it
The reporting view returns correct figures
The role reads the view but cannot write
The pipeline runs within the credit quota

intermediate.summary: For participants who have used Snowflake. Covers micro-partitions and clustering, warehouse scaling, query optimisation, advanced loading and external tables, deep semi-structured handling, streams/tasks/dynamic-table pipelines, RBAC and governance, secure sharing and Snowpark.
prerequisites: Has loaded and queried data in Snowflake
Comfortable with SQL including window functions
Basic Python for the Snowpark day
outcomes: Tune queries and warehouses with the query profile and clustering
Build incremental pipelines with streams, tasks and dynamic tables
Design scalable RBAC and apply masking and row-access policies
Share governed data products and use Snowpark for Python

course_outcomes.outcome: Explain micro-partitions and improve pruning with clustering
Size and scale warehouses, including multi-cluster warehouses
Profile and optimise queries
Load and unload data at scale and query the data lake with external tables
topics: External Tables and the Data Lake

course_outcomes.outcome: Query complex semi-structured data
Speed up queries with materialised views and search optimisation
Capture changes with streams
Orchestrate task graphs
Build declarative pipelines with dynamic tables
Design role-based access
Protect data with masking and row access policies
topics: Governance: Masking and Row Access Policies

course_outcomes.outcome: Share data through secure views and the Marketplace
topics: Secure Views, Sharing and the Marketplace

course_outcomes.outcome: Build data engineering code with Snowpark and deliver a governed near-real-time pipeline

subtopics: Clustering keys and when they help
days.lab_task: On a large table, compare a selective query before and after adding a clustering key, using the query profile to show partitions scanned.
days.deliverable: Before/after query profiles and a recommendation on whether clustering is worth it
checks: Run a selective filter query on an unclustered large table
The profile shows many partitions scanned
Add a clustering key aligned to the filter
Partitions scanned drop for the same query
A credit estimate supports the keep/drop decision
objectives: Add and assess a clustering key

subtopics: Scale out with multi-cluster for concurrency
days.lab_task: Simulate concurrent users on a single-cluster warehouse, then enable multi-cluster auto-scaling and measure queue time improvement.
days.deliverable: A concurrency test with before/after queue times and a sizing decision
checks: Run many concurrent queries on one cluster
Extra clusters start and queuing drops
The concurrency gain justifies the credits, or does not

subtopics: Reading the query profile in detail
Spilling to local and remote storage
Join explosion and exploding GROUP BY
days.lab_task: Take three slow provided queries, diagnose each with the profile (spilling, poor pruning, bad join), and rewrite them to run faster.
days.deliverable: Three optimised queries with before/after timings and the cause of each slowdown
checks: Identify the bottleneck in each query
Each cause (spill, scan, join) is named from the profile
Every query runs faster with the same result
Remote spill is eliminated or explained
objectives: Read a query profile in depth

days.lab_task: Load a partitioned Parquet dataset using schema inference and column matching, then unload a filtered extract back to a stage as partitioned files.
days.deliverable: A loaded table from Parquet and a partitioned unload to a stage
checks: Use INFER_SCHEMA to create the table
Column names and types are detected correctly
Rows load despite column order differences
Unload a filtered extract partitioned by month
One file per month is produced
objectives: Load columnar formats with schema inference

days.topic: External Tables and the Data Lake
subtopics: When to load versus query in place
days.lab_task: Define an external table over partitioned files in cloud storage, add partition columns, and build a materialised view that speeds up a common query.
days.deliverable: An external table with partitions and a materialised view over it
checks: Create the external table with partition columns
New data appears after a metadata refresh
The common query is faster and stays current
objectives: Query a data lake with external tables

subtopics: Arrays of arrays and deep nesting
Performance of VARIANT versus typed columns
Modelling events to a star schema
days.lab_task: Transform a deeply nested JSON event feed into a clean fact-and-dimension model, handling missing fields and arrays of arrays.
days.deliverable: A star-schema model built from nested JSON with documented assumptions
checks: Flatten nested arrays with LATERAL FLATTEN
Grain is one row per leaf item
Nulls are produced, no query errors
Compare VARIANT versus typed query cost
Typed columns are faster for the hot query
objectives: Model events into a star schema

subtopics: Choosing MV vs SOS vs clustering
days.lab_task: For a point-lookup workload, compare a clustering key, a materialised view and the Search Optimization Service, and choose the best option with evidence.
days.deliverable: A comparison table of the three approaches with a justified choice
checks: Enable Search Optimization on the lookup column
Point lookups scan far fewer partitions
Build a materialised view for the aggregate
The aggregate query is faster and auto-maintained
The choice is justified by speed per credit

days.lab_task: Build a CDC flow that captures inserts, updates and deletes from a source table and applies them to a slowly changing dimension with MERGE.
days.deliverable: A working CDC-to-SCD pipeline with correctness checks
checks: Apply inserts, updates and deletes upstream
The stream reports all three change types
The dimension reflects all changes exactly once
Let the stream go stale past retention
The failure mode is detected and explained

subtopics: Scheduling with CRON and time zones
Resuming and suspending a task graph
days.lab_task: Build a three-step task graph (ingest, transform, publish) with a WHEN condition on the stream, and add failure alerting.
days.deliverable: A task DAG with conditional execution and an alert on failure
checks: Children run only after the parent succeeds
Steps skip cleanly when there is no new data
An alert fires and the run is marked failed

days.lab_task: Rebuild yesterday's streams-and-tasks pipeline as a chain of dynamic tables with a one-minute target lag, and compare effort and cost.
days.deliverable: A dynamic-table pipeline with a comparison to the imperative version
checks: Define the dynamic tables with TARGET_LAG
Downstream tables stay within the lag
Results propagate within the target lag
Trade-offs in control versus simplicity are stated

days.lab_task: Design a role model (access roles per schema, functional roles per team), implement it, and run an access review that proves least privilege.
days.deliverable: A documented role model with scripts and an access-review query
checks: Only the schema owner can grant on its objects
No role has more than its intended privileges
objectives: Use managed access schemas and future grants

days.topic: Governance: Masking and Row Access Policies
days.lab_task: Protect a customer table with a masking policy on email and a row access policy that limits rows by region, driven by the querying role.
days.deliverable: A protected table with masking and row policies and proof they work per role
checks: Low-privilege roles see masked emails; admins see raw
Apply the row access policy by region
Each regional role sees only its rows
Tag the PII columns and audit
Tagged columns and policy use appear in account usage
objectives: Govern PII with tags and auditing

days.topic: Secure Views, Sharing and the Marketplace
days.lab_task: Package a governed data product: a secure view with masking, shared through a listing, with a usage query the provider can run.
days.deliverable: A share/listing exposing one governed secure view and a provider usage query
checks: Expose only the secure view in the share
Base tables are not visible to consumers
Confirm masking still applies through the share
Provider can see queries against the share
objectives: Share via secure views and listings

subtopics: When to use Snowpark versus SQL
days.lab_task: Rewrite a multi-step SQL transformation as a Snowpark Python job with a Python UDF for a custom rule, and confirm it pushes down to Snowflake.
days.deliverable: A Snowpark transformation with a UDF and evidence of pushdown
checks: Build the transformation with the DataFrame API
Register and use a Python UDF
The custom rule is applied in-database
Work runs on Snowflake compute, not the client

days.lab_task: Deliver a governed near-real-time pipeline: ingest with Snowpipe, transform with dynamic tables, protect with masking and row policies, and expose a shared secure view within a credit budget.
days.deliverable: A complete governed pipeline with monitoring and a demo
checks: New data reaches the view within the target lag
Masking and row policies hold through the shared view
The pipeline stays within the resource-monitor budget
objectives: Operate within a budget and demo

advanced.summary: For experienced Snowflake engineers and architects. Covers performance and workload isolation at scale, FinOps, advanced governance and classification, replication and failover, clean rooms, Snowpark UDFs/procedures, Streamlit and Native Apps, large-scale pipelines, acceleration services, data quality, migration, security architecture and account reviews.
prerequisites: One or more years working with Snowflake in production
Comfortable with RBAC, pipelines and the query profile
Python experience for Snowpark and app days
outcomes: Architect isolated, high-performance, cost-governed Snowflake platforms
Run governance, privacy, continuity and security programmes
Build Snowpark, Streamlit and Native App data products
Lead migrations and platform architecture reviews

course_outcomes.outcome: Tune performance and isolate workloads at scale
topics: Performance Tuning and Workload Isolation at Scale

course_outcomes.outcome: Run cost optimisation and FinOps
Audit access with advanced governance and access history
Classify sensitive data and protect privacy
Replicate and fail over for business continuity
Collaborate through clean rooms and advanced sharing
Write Snowpark UDFs, UDTFs and stored procedures
topics: Snowpark: UDFs, UDTFs and Stored Procedures

course_outcomes.outcome: Build data apps with Streamlit in Snowflake and Native Apps
topics: Streamlit in Snowflake and Data Apps

course_outcomes.outcome: Build large-scale pipelines and use acceleration services
Monitor data quality and observability
Plan a migration to Snowflake
Design security architecture with network policies and review a platform architecture

days.topic: Performance Tuning and Workload Isolation at Scale
subtopics: Partitioning and clustering for huge tables
days.lab_task: Design a warehouse topology for mixed ETL, BI and ad-hoc workloads on a large account, and prove each workload meets its latency target without starving others.
days.deliverable: A warehouse topology with per-workload SLOs and evidence they are met
checks: Isolate ETL, BI and ad-hoc onto separate warehouses
A heavy ETL job does not slow BI
Apply query acceleration to the ad-hoc warehouse
Large scans speed up within budget
Each workload meets its stated latency

subtopics: Credit attribution by warehouse, role and query tag
days.lab_task: Build a cost dashboard from ACCOUNT_USAGE, attribute spend with query tags, and deliver three changes that cut credits without hurting SLOs.
days.deliverable: A cost dashboard and three implemented savings with measured impact
checks: Attribute spend by query tag and warehouse
No workload breaches its latency target after changes

days.lab_task: Implement tag-based masking across a database so new PII columns are protected automatically, and use ACCESS_HISTORY to produce a column-lineage report.
days.deliverable: Tag-driven governance plus a lineage/access report
checks: Attach masking to a PII tag
A newly tagged column is masked without new policy work
Only aggregated results are allowed for a sensitive table
Build a lineage report from ACCESS_HISTORY
It shows which queries read which PII columns

days.lab_task: Run classification on a new dataset, apply masking from the detected categories, and implement a right-to-erasure request across dependent objects.
days.deliverable: A classified, masked dataset and a documented erasure procedure
checks: PII categories are detected and tagged
Detected PII is masked for analysts
The subject's data is removed from all dependent objects

days.lab_task: Configure a failover group to a second region, set RPO/RTO targets, and run a tested failover and failback with the client redirect.
days.deliverable: A replication/failover setup with a timed, tested failover
checks: Create a failover group and replicate
Objects and policies appear in the target region
Run a failover with client redirect
Clients connect to the secondary without code change
objectives: Operate failover groups and client redirect

days.lab_task: Build a privacy-preserving overlap analysis between two parties using a clean-room pattern, so neither sees the other's raw rows.
days.deliverable: A clean-room overlap analysis with proof that raw rows stay private

days.topic: Snowpark: UDFs, UDTFs and Stored Procedures
days.lab_task: Build a Python UDTF that expands a document into scored sentences and a stored procedure that orchestrates it, with unit tests.
days.deliverable: A tested UDTF and orchestration procedure deployed to Snowflake
checks: It returns one scored row per sentence
It processes a batch and writes results
All tests pass against expected outputs

days.topic: Streamlit in Snowflake and Data Apps
days.lab_task: Build a Streamlit-in-Snowflake app that lets an analyst explore the governed sales data under their own role, respecting masking and row policies.
days.deliverable: A deployed data app that honours the caller's governance
checks: Run the app as two different roles
Each sees only its permitted, masked data
Share the app with a role
Only granted roles can open it

days.lab_task: Package a simple analytics capability as a Native App with a setup script and a versioned release, and install it as a consumer in a test account pattern.
days.deliverable: A versioned native app package with a working install flow
checks: Build the application package and version
The version is listed and installable
The setup script provisions objects in the consumer
The consumer upgrades without data loss
objectives: Install and upgrade as a consumer

subtopics: Partitioning and pruning for pipeline tables
days.lab_task: Design a high-volume ingestion pipeline with a backfill path, idempotent merges, a quarantine for bad records and a replay procedure.
days.deliverable: A scalable pipeline design with backfill, quarantine and replay, implemented on a sample
checks: Run a backfill alongside live ingest
Backfill does not double-count live data
They land in quarantine, not the target
Replay quarantined records after a fix

subtopics: Search Optimization for lookups, substring and geospatial
days.lab_task: For a large multi-tenant workload, decide per query pattern between QAS, SOS, materialised views and clustering, and prove the spend is justified.
days.deliverable: A per-pattern acceleration plan with measured speed-per-credit
checks: Enable the right feature per pattern
Each hot pattern meets its latency target
Feature spend is attributed and bounded

days.lab_task: Add data-quality checks (freshness, null rate, row-count drift) to a pipeline with alerts, and build a data-health dashboard the team can watch.
days.deliverable: Quality checks with alerts and a data-health dashboard
checks: Current data health is visible at a glance

days.lab_task: Plan and execute a sample migration from a legacy warehouse: convert schema and one ETL job, transfer data, and reconcile row and sum checks before cutover.
days.deliverable: A migration runbook with a reconciled sample migration
checks: Convert the schema and one ETL job
The job produces the same output on Snowflake
Reconcile row counts and key sums
Source and target match within tolerance
The runbook has a tested rollback path

subtopics: Network policies and allowed IP lists
days.lab_task: Harden an account: enforce a network policy, key-pair auth for a service user, an MFA/session policy, and a quarterly access-certification query.
days.deliverable: A hardened account configuration with an access-certification report
checks: Connections from outside the allowed list are blocked
Set up key-pair auth for a service user
The service connects without a password
Over-privileged or stale grants are flagged

subtopics: Reviewing an account against best practice
days.lab_task: Review a provided Snowflake account across performance, cost, governance and continuity, and present prioritised findings with a remediation roadmap.
days.deliverable: An architecture-review report with prioritised findings and a roadmap
checks: Assess the four pillars with evidence
Each finding cites a metric or query
Items are ranked by impact and effort
Trade-offs and next steps are clear to a decision-maker
objectives: Review an account against best practice
